# Derived by tools/keycheck.py - do not edit by hand; run it with --accept.
# Each line is a control a mouse can use and a keyboard cannot reach: clickable
# markup that is not a button, a link, a field, or anything carrying tabindex.
# Being here means it is known and not yet fixed. It should shrink; growth is printed.
#
# Three of these are not conversions, and saying so here is the point of a ledger: an entry means
# somebody read it and decided, not that a fix is pending.
#
#   #scrim (both panels) and #v-er (both diagrams) are dismissal surfaces - the backdrop behind a
#   dialog, and the empty canvas around the drawing. Clicking them cancels; they carry no label and
#   fill the viewport. A <button> there would be one enormous tab stop announcing nothing, so what
#   they owe a keyboard is Escape, not focus. Neither panel answers Escape on its dialogs today.
#
#   #pvtable is not a control at all. It holds one delegated listener for every fields table there
#   will ever be, and the thing it acts on - .plbtn - is already a real <button> with aria-expanded.
#   It is recorded because this check keys on the element that carries the handler, and it cannot
#   tell a delegation host from a control. Stated rather than taught: the alternative is a checker
#   that guesses at intent.
